problem_text:
A network of ten relay stations requires a maintenance technician to perform a sequential inspection circuit.  
The geographical positions of the stations (in grid units) are:  
Station Alpha: (75,120)  
Station Beta: (23,47)  
Station Gamma: (27,70)  
Station Delta: (28,142)  
Station Epsilon: (155,176)  
Station Zeta: (39,179)  
Station Eta: (114,102)  
Station Theta: (47,196)  
Station Iota: (107,110)  
Station Kappa: (44,63)  

The cable lengths (in kilometers) connecting pairs of stations are precisely known:  
Alpha–Gamma: 69.3  
Alpha–Delta: 51.9  
Alpha–Epsilon: 97.7  
Alpha–Zeta: 69.1  
Alpha–Eta: 43.0  
Alpha–Theta: 81.0  
Alpha–Iota: 33.5  
Alpha–Kappa: 64.9  
Beta–Gamma: 23.3  
Beta–Delta: 95.1  
Beta–Epsilon: 184.6  
Beta–Zeta: 133.0  
Beta–Eta: 106.3  
Beta–Theta: 150.9  
Beta–Iota: 105.0  
Beta–Kappa: 26.4  
Gamma–Delta: 72.0  
Gamma–Epsilon: 166.2  
Gamma–Zeta: 109.7  
Gamma–Eta: 92.7  
Gamma–Theta: 127.6  
Gamma–Iota: 89.4  
Gamma–Kappa: 18.4  
Delta–Epsilon: 131.5  
Delta–Zeta: 38.6  
Delta–Eta: 94.8  
Delta–Theta: 57.2  
Delta–Iota: 85.2  
Delta–Kappa: 80.6  
Epsilon–Zeta: 116.0  
Epsilon–Eta: 84.6  
Epsilon–Theta: 109.8  
Epsilon–Iota: 81.6  
Epsilon–Kappa: 158.4  
Zeta–Eta: 107.5  
Zeta–Theta: 18.8  
Zeta–Iota: 96.9  
Zeta–Kappa: 116.1  
Eta–Theta: 115.4  
Eta–Iota: 10.6  
Eta–Kappa: 80.1  
Theta–Iota: 104.9  
Theta–Kappa: 133.0  
Iota–Kappa: 78.6  

Due to a permanent outage, no direct cable exists between Station Alpha and Station Beta.  
Furthermore, owing to a switching restriction, the inspection route must incorporate exactly one—and not both—of the following cable segments: the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every station exactly once before returning to the starting point.
